target_customer: Large consumer packaged goods brands and retailers
problem: CPG brands pay heavily for shelf space but cannot easily audit display, price and competitor activity across stores. Milky Way AI offered a computer vision mobile app (InstaShelf) to cut audit time about 10x and cost about 3x, per its YC description.
business_model: B2B SaaS for CPG brands and retailers

founders.name: Eunice Wong
founders.background_notes: YC page: about a decade helping large retailers and brands with customer data science, loyalty programs and cross-border e-commerce payments; no employers named.

founders.name: Sagar Setu
education: PhD in aerospace engineering (university not listed)

investors: Sequoia Capital (Spark Fellowship, per aggregator snippet)

technical_complexity.rationale: Shelf recognition by SKU on phone images needs trained vision models and data collection across stores, hard for five people but a known problem.

defensibility.rationale: Image data could compound, but established shelf-recognition vendors existed and no sourced customers or contracts show lock-in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows a takeover; the company is listed Inactive by YC with cause not public.

market_need_then: The company site cites a 2018 IHL Group estimate that out-of-stock and merchandising problems cost retailers and brands about $1 trillion a year. Its YC description cites $500 billion yearly spent on shelf space.

branding.domain_note: Uses milkyway.ai; later unrelated companies (MilkyWay crypto protocol, Milkyway X AI) share similar names.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic space name with no sourced brand assets, and later collisions with unrelated companies named MilkyWay.

outcome_analysis: Milky Way AI sold a computer vision shelf audit app to CPG brands from Singapore and joined YC in Summer 2021, then received a reported $100K grant in December 2021. YC lists it as inactive but no shutdown, acquisition or post-mortem was found, and the website still shows 2021-dated content, so the cause of the outcome is not public.
notes: Grant round rests on a single database (CB Insights) and the Sequoia Spark attribution on a search snippet. CB Insights total is $430K and PitchBook says $218K, so earlier rounds are unaccounted for and the round list is incomplete. Investors named by databases without round attribution: Peak XV Partners, Diverse Angels, Pacemakers, Samsung NEXT Ventures. Site names no founders. A $5M MilkyWay seed in April 2024 is an unrelated crypto protocol. Competitor lists seen (Trax, Pensa, Scandit) were undated aggregator pages, so none recorded for the 2021 baseline. Founding year 2019 per YC and PitchBook.
